svg.title: How PartnerRide computes the gap between two riders
svg.desc: Animated walkthrough: both Karoos take their own GPS fix stamped with satellite time, broadcast it directly to each other in a 19-byte Bluetooth Low Energy advertisement — no internet, no phone and no server are involved — validate the received packet, dead-reckon the older fix forward to a common evaluation time, and show the resulting signed straight-line distance in the ride data field.
svg.text: PartnerRide — how two Karoos measure the gap
One identical APK on both bikes · both fixes aligned to a single GPS timestamp before the distance is taken

g.text: both devices fix at 1 Hz, but never at the same instant — these two fixes are 1.6 s apart
timestamps are Location.getTime() (satellite UTC), never the device clock — the two clocks drift
advertise ~250 ms · scan duty-cycled, accepted packets land every 2–3 s · manufacturer ID 0xFFFF · no pairing, no connection, no ACK
validated in order — every failure is a silent drop (debug log only, never a crash)
every advertisement is validated before it is allowed to change anything on screen
duplicates of the same fix arrive ~4x a second — the replay guard accepts only a strictly newer timestamp
T_eval = max(12.000 s, 13.600 s) = 13.600 s — A’s fix is 1.6 s older, so A is dead-reckoned forward
8.2 m/s × 1.6 s = 13.1 m along 92° (flat-earth projection, capped at 3 s — beyond that the receiver falls back to timestamp matching)
comparing the two raw fixes without aligning them would read 41 m — 13 m too far
each device takes its own 1 Hz fix,
no pairing, no ACK — both ways
reckon the older fix to T_eval
signed by own heading → data field
